column3: Near-verbatim counterpart: Gardens of Eden, gold bracelets, and silk clothing describe the same eternal reward.
The immediately preceding command to recite revelation provides the passage's framing, but adds little to the reward image itself.
Obedient people join the righteous, offering a limited parallel to the good company implied by the excellent resting place.
Closely repeats the believers' entry into gardens with rivers, gold bracelets, and silk as reward.
Its promised earthly refuge uses the same resting-place root, foreshadowing the later declaration of the truly good resting place.
The surah's opening promise of a good reward for believers doing righteous deeds grounds 18:31's depicted recompense.
It closely parallels the green silk, brocade, and bracelets that materialize paradise's honor and comfort.
The immediate contrast between those seeking God and worldly adornment prepares the eternal adornment granted in 18:31.
Its alternative outcomes in conflict do not clarify the garden reward or its contrast with worldly display.
Gardens of Eden with rivers and whatever the God-conscious desire provide a close reward parallel.
The preceding punishment scene is the direct negative counterpart, ending with the opposite verdict: an evil resting place.
It confirms that those who do good receive the best reward, paradise, and enduring residence, though without the detailed imagery.
Its silk and brocade clothing directly repeats the clothing specified for the garden dwellers.
The immediately prior verse identifies faith and righteous deeds as the work whose unreduced reward 18:31 depicts.
The concise formula that God rewards those who excel supports the recompense principle but supplies no distinctive imagery.
Gardens of Eden, rivers, permanence, and reward for purification closely parallel the focus's enduring recompense.
The next verse opens the parable of two worldly gardens, setting transient possession against the promised eternal gardens.
Its description of excellent women does not materially clarify the focus's reward structure or imagery.
It promises believers Gardens of Eden, rivers, permanence, and divine pleasure, a close expansion of the focus's reward.
The fruitful gardens and river begin the local worldly-garden counterimage, though their transience emerges more fully later.

Forgiveness after replacing wrong with good is not a specific neighbor to the described reward scene.

Reclining on arranged couches offers a clear but partial parallel to the focus's reclined garden dwellers.

The superiority of God's judgment is not a sufficiently specific neighbor to the garden recompense.

Others' resentment at a favorable event does not clarify the focus verse's reward or imagery.

The loss of the garden's water completes the local contrast with the unfailing rivers beneath the eternal gardens.

Viewing from couches in the hereafter partially parallels the focus's reclining-on-couches image.
The ruined garden and the owner's late regret expose the collapse of the worldly adornment contrasted with 18:31.

Pharaoh's promise of nearness to magicians is unrelated to the focus's garden residence.

The bare designation of the companions of the right offers no specific contribution.

The deathbed confession of disbelievers is not a substantive neighbor to the promised reward.
The household-access rule and greeting do not relate to the focus.
Mutual waiting supplies no connection to the garden reward.
The threat of marking an opponent has no usable relation to the focus.

The life of this world is likened to vegetation that dries away, supplying the local transience contrast to the lasting gardens.
Wealth and children are worldly adornment, while enduring righteous deeds are better in reward and hope: the passage's clearest interpretive neighbor.
Faith and righteous deeds receive the Gardens of Paradise as lodging, directly restating the focus's recipients and destination.
Their abiding without desire to depart confirms the permanent, fully satisfactory rest pictured in 18:31.

Obedience leads to entry into a garden with rivers, a direct concise recompense formula.
The God-conscious are in gardens and bliss, supplying the broader setting for the reclining and companionship that follow.
